Seminar Title:

Malware Family Classification from Behavioral API Multigraphs Using Edge-Aware Graph Neural Networks

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Computer Science and Engineering

Speaker Name:

Jena Krishna Priyadarsini Kailash

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Room (CS114)

Date and Time:

06 Nov 2026 11:30 AM

Contact:

Prof. P. Bhattacharjee, PIC, Seminar, CS Dept.

Abstract:

Malware family classification from dynamic analysis traces remains challenging because flat API-call sequences and aggregated feature vectors do not explicitly capture relationships among API calls. In this work, we present a graph-based framework for malware family classification from dynamic behavioral analysis. Each malware execution report generated by the CAPEv2 sandbox is modeled as a directed behavioral API multigraph, where nodes represent unique API names and edges preserve the corresponding call arguments, semantic categories, and execution status. The graphs are classified using an edge-aware graph neural network with message passing, graph attention, residual connections, and dual mean–max pooling. Imbalance aware training and post-hoc threshold calibration are used to address class imbalance. Evaluated on the public Avast-CTU CAPEv2 dataset containing 48,976 samples from ten malware families under a temporal evaluation protocol, the proposed model achieves a macro-F1 score of 94.04% as a single model and 95.25% as a five-model ensemble. A controlled comparison across five graph convolution operators and a component ablation study shows that framework components have a stronger influence on performance than the choice of graph convolution operator, and that hand-crafted graph-level statistics are largely redundant. The interpretability analysis further examines behavioral overlap among misclassified malware families.
